pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Large, irregular polygonal regions with high-contrast, sharp edge gradients. Patch geometry varies from roughly quadrilateral to hexagonal, with a notable reduction in spatial area from the mid-flank toward the posterior region.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Continuous topological network of light-toned pathways separating patches. The network consists of uniform pixel-thickness corridors that meet at clearly defined junction nodes, typically consisting of three-way intersections.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: A low-amplitude, high-frequency jagged silhouette is visible along the dorsal ridge of the neck and shoulder, where mane fibers create a textured boundary against the background.

other_distinctive_markers: A small avian subject (oxpecker) is perched on the posterior rump, creating a localized cluster of dark pixels that disrupts the light pelage corridor.
